note: Each extra test case under a scenario must occupy a different slot. A slot is a distinct condition axis, not a renamed copy of the same test. Code never synthesises clones such as 'variant 2'.

generic_extras.focus: A one- or two-token query that still has a gold relevant set.
A long, multi-clause query that mixes two information needs.
The needed fact lives in a table, list, or numbered procedure rather than prose.
Two near-duplicate documents compete; the test must show which one the metric sees.
An older version and a current version of the same policy are both in the corpus.
The answer requires joining facts from two different knowledge sources.
The query has few or no near neighbours in the index.
The first relevant item sits at exactly rank k of the retriever.

positive.focus: Adjacent chunks from mixed-length policy documents sit inside the overlap band.
Short FAQ chunks that share a heading still overlap inside the band.
Numbered procedure steps chunked sequentially with healthy overlap.

negative.focus: A hard split with no shared tokens between adjacent chunks.
Adjacent chunks are almost copies of each other (overlap far above the band).
Fragments so small they never retrieve and inflate orphan rate / bad overlap.

edge.focus: Configured overlap sits on the lower edge of the pinned band.
Configured overlap sits on the upper edge of the pinned band.
A document that yields only one chunk, so adjacent-pair overlap is undefined or skipped.

positive.focus: The gold relevant chunk is the top hit for a clear factual query.
Several relevant sources appear in top-k without collapsing to one document.
A paraphrased query still retrieves the same gold chunk.

negative.focus: The gold chunk was deleted from the index; retrieval must miss.
High-similarity distractors outrank the true relevant chunk.
A well-formed query whose answer is not in the corpus at all.

edge.focus: The first relevant document sits at exactly rank k.
Two chunks share the same retrieval score; ranking order is the edge.
Only the title overlaps the query; body relevance is weak.

positive.focus: Context assembly keeps the gold relevant passages and drops noise.
Reranking promotes the gold passage into the selected window.
Selected context covers more than one distinct source.

negative.focus: Near-duplicate passages are stuffed into the prompt.
The gold passage was retrieved but not selected into context.
Cached context is reused when the query needs novel content.

edge.focus: Selected tokens sit at the context-window budget.
Half the selected chunks are cached, half are novel.
One selected passage is cited in the answer; another is unused.

positive.focus: A short factoid whose gold answer is a single span in retrieved context.
A gold answer of several sentences that the generator must cover.
A numeric or date fact that must match gold exactly enough for the metric.

negative.focus: The corpus cannot support the question; the system should abstain or fail EM/F1.
Two corpus passages disagree; a single gold cannot be matched cleanly.
A lookalike entity is in context and tempts a wrong answer.

edge.focus: Gold and a correct paraphrase differ lexically (EM vs semantic).
The answer is a correct subset of the gold span.
Gold is a list of items; order and completeness are the edge.

positive.focus: Every claim in the answer has a supporting span in retrieved context.
The answer restates a procedure that is present verbatim in context.
Support for the answer is split across two retrieved passages.

negative.focus: The answer adds a statistic that is not in context.
The answer contradicts a retrieved passage.
The model answers from parametric knowledge while retrieved context is silent.

edge.focus: A multi-claim answer with one unsupported clause at the threshold.
Hedged wording ('may', 'typically') still asserts an unsupported fact.
A true detail that happens to be absent from this retrieved set.

positive.focus: Each citation resolves to a supporting span in retrieved context.
Citations name more than one source and each is used.
A quoted phrase in the answer maps to the cited chunk.

negative.focus: A citation points at a document or span that was not retrieved.
Passages are cited but never used in the answer.
The citation names the right document but a non-supporting span.

edge.focus: A single claim is over-cited to two passages, only one of which supports it.
Only some answer tokens have citation support (attribution coverage edge).
Citation plus a reasoning trace; domain policy may be required.

adversarial.focus: A user query that tries to override system policy in the prompt.
A retrieved document contains hidden instructions for the generator.
A role-play jailbreak that should still be refused after retrieval.

security.focus: A poisoned corpus snippet attempts a policy override via retrieval.
The query tries to extract system prompt or index internals.
A query crafted to pull another tenant or user's retrieved context.

negative.focus: A legitimate policy question must not be blocked by safety filters.
A benign 'how do we reset access' question that looks similar to an attack.
The corpus mentions a public office-holder name that is not a leakage failure.

monitoring.focus: Measure the metric on the pinned eval query set in the eval environment.
Repeat queries that should hit cache if caching is enabled.
First-seen queries with a cold cache.

regression.focus: Compare this run's telemetry to the last signed eval run.
Re-measure after a declared prompt-template version change.
Re-measure after a declared index rebuild.

monitoring.focus: Compute the lifecycle metric over the declared current monitoring window.
Logs that match the declared schema versus logs with missing fields.
TEVV planned tests versus tests actually executed in the window.

regression.focus: Recompute after a declared corpus refresh event.
Recompute after a generator or embedder version change.
Recompute after a safety or retrieval-policy change.
